steps.text: Set your limits, pick a trading mode and let the demo build your confidence first.

pros: Funding by card, transfer, PayPal and Skrill.
cons: The demo claim buried in the signup flow.
Performance examples without dates or proof.
Asset list that shifts between pages.
The headline fee claim and the real cost disagree.
redFlags: No regulator, licence or audit named anywhere.
Marketing numbers the fine print quietly qualifies.
A support bullet that garbles two claims at once.

faqs.a: Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.
The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.
The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.

bottomLine: The desk, the demo and the funding options all check out. The score reflects the paperwork around them.
We rate it 4.2 with conditions: the platform is usable, the published claims are not all verifiable, and the US$300 minimum is the right size for testing either.
